title: Stability and instability analysis of resonance-induced nonlinear bound states
authors: Jackson C. Turner, Michael I. Weinstein
abstract: We study the focusing one-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger / Gross--Pitaevskii equation (NLS-GP), where the potential of the underlying linear Schrödinger operator, $H_V=-\partial_x^2+V(x)$, is compactly supported. In \cite{turner2026resonance} the authors proved that purely imaginary zeros (transmission resonances) or purely imaginary poles in the lower half plane (scattering resonances) of a reflection coefficient of $H_V$ seed branches of {\it resonance-induced nonlinear bound states}, and that these states bifurcate at a strictly positive $L^2(\mathbb R)$ excitation threshold. This is in contrast to nonlinear bound states which bifurcate at zero $L^2$-norm from point spectra of $H_V$ (corresponding to poles in the upper half plane). In this paper we establish precise criteria for the nonlinear orbital stability and instability of the resonance-induced states near the bifurcation point. A corollary is that resonance-induced nonlinear states are orbitally stable if i) the underlying linear (scattering or transmission) resonance frequency is sufficiently small, and ii) the corresponding linear resonance eigenmode is strictly positive. Numerical simulations are presented to explore regimes not accessible to our theory, and to explore the large time dynamics for initial conditions near stable and unstable resonance-induced nonlinear bound states.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the orbital stability and instability of nonlinear bound states that emerge from linear scattering or transmission resonances in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. By developing criteria based on resonance eigenproperties, it provides a powerful mathematical tool to predict the long-time behavior of such quantum systems. This is highly relevant for understanding nonlinear wave phenomena in physical systems like Bose-Einstein condensates or optical fibers.
main_problem: The paper establishes precise criteria for determining the nonlinear orbital stability and instability of bound states that are induced by linear scattering or transmission resonances.
main_result:
The stability of these resonance-induced states is determined by the signs of two quantities, $\Omega^\star$ and $
u^\star$, requiring $\Omega^\star > 0$ and $
u^\star < 0$ for orbital stability near the bifurcation point.
method: The analysis uses bifurcation theory applied to the nonlinear Schrödinger/Gross-Pitaevskii equation, analyzing the spectral properties of linearized operators associated with the resonance eigenpairs.
model_or_system: The system is the focusing one-dimensional cubic nonlinear Schrödinger/Gross-Pitaevskii equation ($i\partial_t\Psi = -\partial_x^2\Psi + V(x)\Psi -|\Psi|^2\Psi$). The analysis focuses on nonlinear bound states bifurcating from linear scattering or transmission resonances associated with the underlying linear operator $H_V = -\partial_x^2 + V(x)$.
key_observables:
The $L^2$ norm of the state, $N[\psi] = \|\psi\|^2_{L^2}$, and the stability indicators $\Omega^\star$ and $
u^\star$.
important_parameters: The resonance frequency ($\gamma_\star$), the bifurcation parameter ($\epsilon$), and the potential parameters defining the resonance (e.g., $	au$ in later sections).
main_assumptions:
The analysis assumes the non-degeneracy condition $B^\star 
eq 0$ and is valid for small bifurcation parameters $\epsilon$ or small perturbation parameters $	au$.

Figure 2.1 illustrates different bifurcation scenarios (point spectrum, SR, TR) in the $k$-plane and the $(N, E)$-plane. Later figures track the evolution of stability terms ($\Omega^\star,

paper_structure:
The paper first establishes the general framework for resonance-induced states, detailing the stability criteria based on $\Omega^\star$ and $
u^\star$. It then applies this framework to specific potentials, including those derived from Pöschl-Teller potentials, and extends the analysis to continuous families of potentials using perturbation theory.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools to characterize the stability of nonlinear structures (like solitons or breathers) whose existence is fundamentally linked to the spectral properties (resonances) of the underlying linear operator, which is crucial in quantum optics and nonlinear wave physics.
